Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Namibia's NPRS fully integrates civil registration (births, deaths, marriages) with the identity system. The CRVSID system uniquely integrates identity management with the population register—identity cards are legally issued directly from the national population register. E-birth and e-death notification platforms link health facilities to the NPRS in real time. The UIN (Unique Identity Number) connects all modules. The UN CRVSID case study describes Namibia as having a 'fully integrated civil registration and identity management system.' Value=3 (Full).

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance and Public Enterprises (MFPE) was co-lead on the UNDP Digital Finance Ecosystem Assessment and Strategy 2023, which encompassed digital identity as part of the digital public infrastructure framework. The Ministry of Finance has interest in ensuring electronic transactions for public services are safe and reliable. Budget allocations for MHAISS (N$7.4 billion) include N$70 million for e-ID rollout and N$178 million for civil registration (2025/26). Finance oversight appears partial rather than full. Value=2 (Partial).

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The NPRS was fully digitised by 2017 and is an electronic, web-based enterprise system. All local registration centres are connected to the NPRS in real time. E-birth and e-death notification platforms link health facilities to the central database. M-files database holds ~2.7 million digitised birth records. The World Bank 2016 report confirmed 4.7 million records digitised and full digitalisation completed by May 2016. Value=3 (Digital).

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Namibia's NPRS uses NamX (National Data Exchange Service Bus / X-Road based interoperability layer), enabling the population register to link with functional public and private sector registries including social welfare, electoral, health, banking and taxation systems. The NPRS links birth/death/marriage modules via Unique Identity Number (UIN) and is described as interoperable in multiple World Bank and UN case studies. The 2019 ID4Africa presentation confirms the Government of Namibia Interoperability (IOP) Framework and NamX data exchange platform. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The first national ID card is provided free of cost to all eligible applicants. The MHAISS website confirms: 'Application: Free.' The UN CRVSID case study explicitly states 'the first card is provided free of cost.' Duplicate/replacement IDs incur fees (N$150 incremental) but the initial credential is free. Value=1 (No cost for first issuance; note scale: 1=No, meaning no cost barrier for initial credential).

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Namibia and Botswana signed an agreement (launched February 2023) recognising each other's national ID cards as travel documents for cross-border movement, eliminating the need for passports between the two countries. Veridos (2023) and APC (2024) confirm this bilateral arrangement. The SADC regional DPI initiative (2025) is developing a federated eKYC ecosystem across 16 SADC states. Currently only the Namibia-Botswana bilateral recognition is in effect; SADC-wide interoperability is under development. Value=2 (Some regional).

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: The 2023 Namibia Population and Housing Census found that 85.4% of the population aged 16+ were issued with a National Identification Card (Namibian ID). The UN CRVSID case study (2023) citing World Bank data reports 91% coverage of ID among population aged 15+. The 2016 intercensal survey showed 83.7% in possession of ID cards. Coverage is firmly in the 70-89% range. Value=4 (70-89%).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: Since January 2023, SIM card registration is mandatory in Namibia under the Communications Act (Section 77) and CRAN regulations. Customers must present a government-issued ID (national ID card or passport) to register SIM cards. Unregistered SIM cards were deactivated after the March 2024 deadline. Telecom Namibia deactivated ~200,000 unregistered SIM cards. National ID is the primary document used for mandatory SIM registration. Value=3 (Mandatory).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID is mandatory for accessing social grants in Namibia. The UN CRVSID case study confirms ID is required for social grants, school admission, and government services. Biometric verification against the Namibian ID is used for social grant payments (fingerprint verification for welfare recipients, including veteran benefits). The NPRS was used to validate identity for COVID-19 emergency income support. Social grants are linked to ID registration. Value=3 (Mandatory).
